extracted.intended_audience: NSF proposers, award recipients, institutional research administrators, and NSF staff
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative NSF policies and procedural guidance for preparing and submitting proposals and for award issuance, administration, and monitoring across NSF assistance programs. Covers proposal eligibility, allowable activities, award instruments, financial and administrative requirements, and institutional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAPPG implements 2 CFR §200
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAPPG, in conjunction with the applicable standard award conditions incorporated by reference in the award, serve as the Foundation’s implementation of 2 CFR §200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PAPPG and the award conditions are silent on an area covered by 2 CFR §200, the requirements in 2 CFR §200 must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow program solicitations when they modify PAPPG
rubrics_metrics.description: Some NSF programs have program solicitations that modify the general provisions of the PAPPG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a solicitation modifies PAPPG provisions, the guidelines in that solicitation must be followed instead of the general PAPPG language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NSF Grants.gov Application Guide for Grants.gov submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy and procedural guidance contained in the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide should be followed when preparing and submitting proposals to NSF via Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Grants.gov Application Guide for technical and procedural requirements for Grants.gov submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAPPG scope excludes procurement contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAPPG does not apply to NSF procurement contracts, other arrangements, or other transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NSF contracts or other arrangements, consult guidance maintained by the Division of Acquisition and Cooperative Support (DACS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible proposers and proposal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF considers proposals submitted by organizations on behalf of individuals or groups for support in most single, multi-, cross-, trans- and inter- disciplinary fields of STEM research and education convergence research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories of eligible proposers are detailed in Chapter I.E; consult program-specific pages and funding opportunities for additional eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities NSF does not normally support (eligibility exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF does not normally support technical assistance, pilot plant efforts, research requiring security classification, the development of products for commercial marketing, or market research for a particular project or invention. Biological research on mechanisms of disease in humans, including on the etiology, diagnosis, or treatment of disease or disorder, is normally not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: research that advances knowledge in engineering, mathematical, physical, computer, or information sciences with etiology/diagnosis/treatment-related goals may be eligible; bioengineering and assistive information technology research to aid persons with disabilities is eligible. Use NSF Funding/Awards search to check program fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF recognizes and highly encourages leadership, partnership, and contributions from individuals and institutions from communities that are underrepresented and/or underserved in STEM in all NSF opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF expects equitable and inclusive treatment in proposal and award processes and encourages demographically diverse institutions (e.g., community colleges, HBCUs, TCUs, women's colleges, institutions serving persons with disabilities, PUIs, MSIs, HSIs) to lead or partner on proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients are responsible for project conduct and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are wholly responsible for conducting their project activities and preparing the results for publication and/or other forms of dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF does not assume responsibility for findings or their interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An AOR/Authorized Representative is the administrative official empowered to make certifications and representations on behalf of the proposing organization and can commit the organization to the conduct of a project and adherence to NSF policies and award requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals require institutional certification/representations by an AOR; institutions must ensure appropriate authority and review before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and distinctions: Grant Agreement vs Cooperative Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant Agreement: legal instrument to transfer value to carry out a public purpose, distinguished from cooperative agreement by lack of substantial NSF involvement. Cooperative Agreement: similar legal instrument but provides for substantial involvement between NSF and recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grants where minimal NSF involvement is needed; use cooperative agreements when substantial, ongoing Foundation involvement is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Grant vs Continuing Grant definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Grant: NSF provides specific support for a specified period with no statement of intent to provide additional support. Continuing Grant: provides specific support for an initial period with a statement of intent to provide additional support for additional periods if funds/results warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award type has implications for funding expectations and proposal planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Reimbursement vs Fixed Amount Award definitions and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Reimbursement Award: NSF reimburses recipient for allowable costs incurred up to the award amount; accountability is based on technical progress and financial/fiscal reporting. Fixed Amount Award: NSF provides a specific level of support without regard to actual costs; accountability is based primarily on performance and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed amount awards reduce administrative burden; cost allowability must follow applicable cost principles (see 2 CFR §200).

rubrics_metrics.name: PI and co-PI personnel limits on proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal submitted to NSF must include a PI and a maximum of four co-PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the PAPPG, the term Principal Investigator also includes Project Director and co-Principal Investigator includes co-Project Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient definition and award targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient means an entity that receives an award directly from NSF and does not include subrecipients or individuals that are beneficiaries of the award; NSF awards are normally made to organizations rather than to the PI or co-PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure organizational eligibility and appropriate institutional approvals when routing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF-Recipient relationship obligations under grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Under grants, NSF agrees to provide up to a specified amount of financial support; the recipient agrees to perform the project as proposed, prudently manage funds, and carry out activities in accordance with award provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter VI.B for documents that comprise an NSF award; recipients must meet award terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for using cooperative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative agreements are used when accomplishment of project objectives requires substantial ongoing NSF involvement during performance (technical and/or managerial complexity requiring close coordination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial involvement areas include prior agency approval requirements, frequency/type of project plans, special reporting, and project and recipient reviews. NSF may provide technical/management advice and may require prior approvals of decisions, milestones, or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of projects suitable for cooperative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management of research centers, large curriculum projects, multi-user facilities, projects involving complex subcontracting, construction or operations of major in-house university facilities and major instrumentation development, and projects in which NSF participates with other stakeholder agencies that influence project direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cooperative agreements for projects needing substantive NSF collaboration/oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative agreement instruments: Standalone CA and Master CA/CSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Standalone Cooperative Agreement: single unified award. Master Cooperative Agreement/Cooperative Support Agreement (CA/CSA): master agreement with separate specific awards (CSAs) funded individually under the umbrella master agreement; CSAs have distinct award numbers and funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master CA defines overall provisions; CSAs have additional specific terms and cannot attach funding to the master CA itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: MREFC funding and segregation of construction vs operating costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative agreements for construction are generally funded through the Major Research Equipment and Facilities Construction (MREFC) appropriation; MREFC funds cannot be co-mingled with funds for activities other than construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF issues a separate award for operations/other related activities; recipient must maintain an accounting system capable of segregating MREFC and operating costs and ensure proper application of such costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF right to suspend or terminate awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF retains the right to unilaterally suspend or terminate support for cause or consider termination in accordance with Chapter XII if it is in the best interest of NSF or the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This right applies regardless of cooperative agreement classification; recipients should be aware of terms and conditions that enable such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGA responsibilities and delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Grants & Agreements (DGA) is responsible for award and administration of most NSF assistance awards and conducts pre-award through closeout reviews to ensure compliance with award terms and federal rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants and Agreements Officers have delegated warrant authority to issue awards, issue amendments, certain post-award prior approvals, monitor compliance, and close out awards; their approval constitutes a legal obligation of Federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIAS functions and Policy Office role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Institution & Award Support (DIAS) develops and implements proposal and award policies and procedures, clears NSF funding opportunities, conducts advanced monitoring, cost analysis, audit resolution, and electronic award systems administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Policy Office issues pre- and post-award policies, interprets NSF policies and electronic systems, coordinates outreach, and provides official clearance for funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Analysis and Pre-award (CAP) Branch criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: CAP specializes in determinations regarding the allowability, allocability and reasonableness of costs budgeted or claimed under NSF awards and evaluates accounting systems and internal controls of prospective/current recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAP performs pre-award reviews of new recipients, Phase II small business projects, large-scale award budgets, and indirect cost rate negotiation; provides guidance related to its responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution and Advanced Monitoring (RAM) Branch criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: RAM evaluates the allowability, allocability and reasonableness of costs claimed, evaluates accounting systems/internal controls of current recipients, and conducts audit resolution and advanced monitoring to assess administrative capability, performance, and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAM reviews certain post-award adjustments to expenditures and provides related guidance to recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems Office role in business rules and electronic systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The Systems Office designs, implements, administers and oversees business rules for assistance awards across NSF electronic corporate systems and develops system analysis and requirements for award business rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow electronic system business rules; consult Systems Office guidance for technical/systemic questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DACS acquisition and infrastructure responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Acquisition and Cooperative Support (DACS) provides acquisition, contracts, other arrangements and cooperative agreement award solutions; the Infrastructure Support Branch (ISB) handles cooperative agreements focused on major facilities and participates in project teams, risk assessments, advanced cost analysis and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISB Grants and Agreements Officers have delegated warrant authority for issuing awards related to infrastructure; consult DACS for contract/transaction guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFM financial policy and recipient business relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Financial Management (DFM) is responsible for NSF financial policy, financial management, recipient business office relationships, and vendor payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Payments and Analytics Branch assists recipient financial/business officials with payment and financial reporting matters (see Chapter VIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Infrastructure Office (RIO) oversight and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: RIO is NSF's primary resource for oversight practices related to mid-scale and major facility projects and the NSF-wide resource on project management best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIO provides assistance on project planning, budgeting, implementation, assurance that applicable requirements are followed, and facilitates best practices and lessons learned application across NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the General Counsel (OGC) legal advice
rubrics_metrics.description: OGC provides legal advice and counsel on aspects of Foundation programs, policies, and operations including assistance awards, ethics/conflicts of interest, FOIA, Privacy Act, labor/personnel law, environmental law, fiscal/administrative law, and international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OGC for legal interpretation and issues affecting proposal/award actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Equity and Civil Rights (OECR) compliance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: OECR administers Foundation policies and procedures related to external equal opportunity and civil rights and ensures compliance with Federal EEO and civil rights laws; it responds to civil rights matters for NSF programs or activities receiving Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECR is the authority for notifications required by NSF terms regarding sexual harassment, other harassment, or sexual assault (see Chapter XI.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Inspector General (OIG) oversight and misconduct investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: OIG conducts audits, reviews, and investigations of NSF programs and organizations/individuals that apply for or receive NSF funding; investigates allegations of research misconduct (plagiarism, falsification, fabrication) and other wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG audits focus on award financial/administrative activities; investigations can result in criminal, civil, or administrative sanctions. Report suspected misconduct via OIG hotline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and reviewer anonymity/transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF uses advisors from the scientific and engineering communities (approximately 50,000 annually) to serve on committees or as ad hoc reviewers of proposals; Principal Investigators receive unattributed verbatim copies of peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers and division directors oversee integrity of merit review; reviewers are used to evaluate scientific, technical, and educational merit (see Chapter III for detailed Merit Review Process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance Listings mapping to SAM.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF programs are listed on SAM.gov under specific assistance listings (e.g., 47.041 Engineering, 47.049 Mathematical and Physical Sciences, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SAM.gov assistance listings to find public descriptions and CFDA-equivalent information for NSF programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program definition and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program includes programs/positions/activities that provide compensation or other remuneration from a foreign country/entity in exchange for activities such as unauthorized transfer of IP/data, recruitment, establishing labs or employment that violate federal award terms, inability to terminate agreements, required overlap with federal awards, omission of acknowledgments, nondisclosure to federal sponsors, or conflicts of interest/commitment. It also includes programs sponsored by specified lists (per John S. McCain NDAA provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAPPG lists specific activities (i–ix) that characterize such programs and notes that certain scholarly activities, conference participation, and advising students are not considered malign programs unless funded/organized/managed by entities on the specified lists.
